headline: The Louvre reopens its jewel room empty

sources.title: Louvre Reopens Apollo Gallery Nine Months After Jewel Heist
Louvre's Apollo Gallery Reopens With No Jewelry on Display After Heist
Louvre reopens Apollo Gallery after brazen heist, with no jewels on display
Louvre reopens Apollo Gallery after brazen heist, but no jewels on display (video, AP Archive)

chunks.text: The Louvre in Paris {{opened up}} its Apollo [[Gallery]] again on July 22, nine months after four [[thieves]] {{made off with}} eight pieces of the French [[crown jewels]]. The gallery is one of the most [[decorated]] rooms in the museum, with a painted [[ceiling]] and long glass [[cases]] along the walls. Visitors can walk [[the length of]] it [[once more]]. The cases have nothing in them.

verbs.why: Open up means to make a place available to the public again, usually after repairs or a closure. The Louvre opened up its Apollo Gallery nine months after the theft.

verbs.wrong: To hide in a nearby building
verbs.why: Make off with means to steal something and successfully escape with it. Four thieves made off with eight pieces of the French crown jewels.

chunks.text: The [[robbery]] in October 2025 lasted about seven minutes. The thieves {{pulled up}} a [[basket lift]] against the outside wall, cut a second-floor window open with an [[angle grinder]], and were gone before guards could {{cut off}} the exit. They {{got away with}} a [[sapphire]] necklace once worn by the [[stepdaughter]] of Napoleon Bonaparte, an [[emerald]] necklace holding more than a thousand diamonds, and a [[tiara]] that had belonged to Empress Eugenie. The tiara was damaged as the thieves {{ran off}}, and is now being repaired.

verbs.why: Pull up means to bring a vehicle to a stop right beside something, like a curb or a wall. The thieves pulled up a lift against the museum's outside wall.

verbs.wrong: To close a building to visitors
verbs.why: Cut off means to block a route so nobody can get in or out. Guards could not cut off the thieves' escape before they disappeared.
Get away with here means to escape while carrying something stolen. The thieves got away with two necklaces and a valuable tiara.
Run off means to leave a place quickly, often to escape trouble. The tiara was damaged when the thieves ran off with the jewels.

chunks.text: None of the eight pieces have been [[recovered]]. Two [[suspects]] have told [[investigators]] that somebody else planned the robbery, and that person has not been {{tracked down}}. A government report criticized the museum's [[security]] [[in detail]]. The director at the time {{stepped down}}. The new director has decided that the crown jewels which remain will be {{shut away}} in a [[vault]] with no windows [[rather than]] {{put back}} on [[display]]. France's culture minister called the robbery a [[trauma]] for the whole world.

verbs.wrong: To have a name made public
verbs.why: Track down means to find someone or something after a long, careful search. Investigators still have not tracked down the person who planned the robbery.

verbs.wrong: To be blamed for a mistake
verbs.why: Step down means to leave an important position, often after criticism or pressure. The museum's director stepped down after a report criticized its security.

verbs.correct: To keep in a locked place
verbs.wrong: To be repaired out of public view
verbs.why: Shut away means to keep something locked out of view for safety. The Louvre will shut away its remaining jewels in a windowless vault.

verbs.wrong: To be moved to another museum
verbs.why: Put back means to return an object to the place it came from. Notice the word order: we say put them back, not put back them.

chunks.text: That decision is the real news here, and it is not a comfortable one. A museum exists to show things to the public, and the Louvre has chosen safety over display for objects the public owns. Anyone who {{turns up}} at the Apollo Gallery this summer sees the room itself, the ceiling, the light through the tall windows, and [[a row of]] empty glass cases where the jewels used to be.

verbs.wrong: To buy a ticket in advance
verbs.why: Turn up means to arrive somewhere, often without a fixed schedule. Visitors who turn up at the gallery this summer will see empty glass cases.

mainIdea.s: The Louvre reopened its Apollo Gallery on July 22, nine months after eight crown jewels were stolen. None have been found, so it now locks the remaining jewels in a vault instead of on display.
mainIdea.why: The gallery reopened on July 22, but none of the eight stolen jewels have been recovered. The museum chose to lock the remaining jewels in a vault instead of putting them back on display.

mainIdea.s: Investigators recovered most of the eight stolen crown jewels, but two pieces are still missing after months of searching. The Louvre reopened the gallery on July 22, nine months after the theft.
mainIdea.why: The article says none of the eight jewels have been recovered, not most of them. Two suspects have been questioned, but every piece is still missing.

mainIdea.s: The Louvre separately announced a renovation of its Egyptian wing, due to start next year. The project will close several rooms for up to three years and cost tens of millions of euros.
mainIdea.why: This is about a separate renovation project for the Egyptian wing, not the jewel theft or the empty gallery.
